about: The main tour of Mission 01: one question to Qwen3.8 27B on the DGX Spark, from the file on the SSD to the last word, slowed down. Read by kit/tour.js. Every number is a metric the mission computes from labs/data ({k} in the words, k in a chip), never typed here. state.t is seconds since you hit enter (negative while the model loads), state.slow how many times slower than real time the clock runs.
title: The life of one answer

short.hook: Watch *one answer* travel through my AI box
short.lesson: Every word crosses the memory bus: the GPU waits at {busyWrite}
short.next: Next: the bigger model that writes faster

steps.title: The file wakes up
text: Before you type a word, {model} is a file on the SSD: {weightsGB} of numbers.
Loading copies every one of them into the memory chips, where the GPU can reach them.
On {the} that takes {loadS}.
steps.metaphor: Think of it as unpacking a whole library onto the shelves before the first reader walks in.

breakIt.label: load Qwen3.8-Max
breakIt.caption: The file is bigger than the memory. Nothing runs.

steps.caption: The model starts as a file on the SSD.

steps.title: Every cell is a gigabyte
text: Each glowing square on the memory chips stands for one gigabyte.
{model} fills {cells} of the {usableGB} this machine can give it.
The model stays there the whole time. Nothing has been computed yet.
steps.metaphor: Think of it as a warehouse where every shelf holds exactly one gigabyte.

breakIt.label: make it 16-bit
breakIt.caption: Full size, the same model fills over three times the cells.

steps.caption: Each lit square is one gigabyte of the model.

steps.title: Words become tokens
text: You ask: why does my GPU feel slow?
With the chat template and its instructions that becomes {promptTokens}: pieces of words, each one a number.
They come in through the port and wait in memory for the GPU.
steps.metaphor: Think of it as a typesetter breaking your sentence into pieces of type.

breakIt.label: paste a 30-page document
breakIt.caption: A long document turns the blink of reading into seconds.

steps.caption: Your question becomes tokens: small pieces of words.

steps.title: The engine at full power
text: Reading is math, and the GPU does it for all of your tokens at once.
Every block on the chip lights up. This is the only time it works flat out.
{The} reads at {readTps}.
steps.metaphor: Think of it as a print shop running every press at the same time.

breakIt.label: paste a 30-page document
breakIt.caption: Thousands of tokens keep every block busy for seconds.

steps.caption: Reading your question: every GPU block works at once.

steps.title: One word, the whole model
text: Writing is different. To pick each next word, the GPU needs every weight in the model.
So for every single word, all {perTokenGB} crosses from the memory to the chip.
One word takes {msPerToken}.
steps.metaphor: Think of it as rereading the whole encyclopedia to write one word.

breakIt.label: make it 16-bit
breakIt.caption: Full size: more bytes to move for every single word.

steps.caption: Every word costs one trip through the whole model.

steps.title: The jammed fuel line
text: The memory bus is the road between the memory chips and the GPU.
On {the} it carries {bw}, and while the model writes it is {busWrite} busy.
That road, not the GPU, sets the writing speed.
steps.metaphor: Think of it as a rocket engine fed through one narrow fuel line.

breakIt.label: use an RTX 5090
breakIt.caption: A wider, faster bus delivers the model sooner: words come faster.

steps.caption: The memory bus runs flat out. It sets the speed.

steps.title: The engine waits at {busyWrite}
text: Between deliveries the GPU has almost nothing to do.
Its math takes a sliver of every step: {busyWrite} of what it could do.
It draws {powerWriteW} while it writes, about what it drew while reading.
steps.metaphor: Think of it as a sports car stuck behind a slow truck.

breakIt.label: make it 16-bit
breakIt.caption: More bytes per word, and the GPU waits even longer.

steps.caption: The GPU finishes its math in a flash, then waits.

steps.title: The notes pile up
text: As it writes, the model keeps notes on every token so far: the prompt memory.
Each new token adds {kvKB}, next to the weights.
For this question that is {kvGB}. A long prompt makes the pile much bigger.
steps.metaphor: Think of it as sticky notes the model leaves for itself, one per word.

breakIt.label: feed it a whole codebase
breakIt.caption: A whole codebase: the notes now fill gigabytes.

steps.caption: Each word leaves a note behind. The notes pile up.

steps.title: What if only a slice is read?
text: {model} is a mixture of experts: it keeps {totalB} parameters but reads only {activeB} for each word.
A few cells flash per word instead of all of them.
On {the} it writes {writeTps}: {moeX} as fast as the dense 27B.
steps.metaphor: Think of it as a library where each question needs only one aisle.

breakIt.label: go back to the dense 27B
breakIt.caption: Dense again: every word reads every cell.

steps.caption: A mixture of experts reads a slice, so words come faster.

steps.title: 32 riders, one trip
text: Serve 32 questions at once, and every trip over the bus feeds all of them.
The GPU finally gets some work: {busyWrite} of its math.
Together they get {totalTps}, and each one still gets {writeTps}.
steps.metaphor: Think of it as a bus: the trip costs the same with one rider or thirty-two.

breakIt.label: one rider
breakIt.caption: One rider: the same trip now carries a single word.

steps.caption: Thirty-two answers share every trip across the bus.

steps.title: The answer leaves the port
text: Each finished word goes out through the port as text.
The {answerTokens} of the answer take {writeS} to write.
From the moment you hit enter to the last word: {doneS}.
steps.metaphor: Think of it as a ticker tape feeding out one word at a time.

breakIt.label: paste a 30-page document
breakIt.caption: Reading a long document first makes you wait longer.

steps.caption: Word by word, the answer streams out to you.

steps.title: Mission Report
text: The same question and the same model on five machines.
Writing speed follows the memory bus. Reading follows the math.
Measured on the Spark, reported by others where they published runs, estimated where nobody has.
steps.metaphor: Think of it as five rockets with the same fuel and different fuel lines.

breakIt.label: ask Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
breakIt.caption: A much bigger model: the fastest card cannot even load it.

steps.caption: Same question, five machines: the fastest memory bus wins.
